newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sees growing local money market trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sees growing local money market trading.

text.p: Indonesian central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said on Thursday the value of domestic money market trading was rising at an ever increasing rate.

Djiwandono said in a speech at the launch of the new Reuters "Money 3000" and "Treasury 3000" products in Indonesia that value of the currency traded on the domestic market had risen to 25 trillion rupiah per day from five trillion rupiah four years ago.
He said the value of trading on the foreign exchange market had risen to $9 billion per day from $5 billion per day in 1995.

"Fast development of funds by the financial institutions is important to support business circles. Therefore in the years to come, in line with the demands of development, the procurement of big funds need to be boosted," Djiwandono said.
"To support that step, efficient and healthy financial sector development needs to be made," he said.
The integration of Indonesia's money market had created challenges for those managing Indonesian monetary policy.

"One thing that we can not avoid is the process of integration, in fact, it is difficult to protect ourselves from the turmoil abroad," Djiwandono said, using the example of the Mexico crisis in 1994 which spilled over onto the Indonesian rupiah.
